steps.title: Creating a List
steps.task: Create a list called `colours` containing `"red"`, `"green"`, and `"blue"`.
steps.description:
# Lists

A **list** holds many values in one variable, inside square brackets `[]`.

```python
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]
print(fruits)
```

Use `len()` to count how many items are in the list:

```python
print(len(fruits))  # 3
```

steps.title: Getting Items
steps.example:
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]
print(fruits[0])   # first
print(fruits[1])   # second
print(fruits[-1])  # last
steps.task: You have `animals = ["cat", "dog", "fish"]`. Set `first` to the first animal and `last` to the last animal using indexes.

quiz.question: For pets = ["cat", "dog", "fish"], what is pets[0]?
quiz.explanation: Index 0 is always the first item in the list.

tests.name: first == "cat"
tests.msg: first should be "cat" — the item at index 0

steps.description:
# Getting Items — Indexes

Each item has a number called an **index**. The first item is always index `0`.

```python
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]
print(fruits[0])  # "apple"
print(fruits[1])  # "banana"
```

Use `-1` to get the last item:

```python
print(fruits[-1])  # "cherry"
```

steps.title: Adding Items
steps.example:
animals = ["cat"]
print("Before:", animals)

animals.append("dog")
animals.append("fish")
print("After:", animals)
steps.task: Start with `cart = []`. Use `.append()` to add `"bread"`, `"milk"`, and `"eggs"` — in that order.

quiz.question: What does animals.append("rabbit") do?
quiz.explanation: .append(x) always adds x to the end of the list.

steps.description:
# Adding Items — append

Use `.append()` to add one item to the end of a list.

```python
animals = ["cat", "dog"]
animals.append("fish")
print(animals)  # ["cat", "dog", "fish"]
```

steps.title: Changing Items
steps.example:
colours = ["red", "green", "blue"]
print("Before:", colours)

colours[0] = "pink"
print("After:", colours)
steps.task: You have `pets = ["cat", "dog", "fish"]`. Change the item at index `1` to `"hamster"`.

quiz.question: What does colours[0] = "yellow" do?
options: Replaces the item at index 0 with "yellow"
quiz.explanation: Index assignment replaces the item at that position.

steps.description:
# Changing Items

Replace any item by assigning to its index:

```python
pets = ["cat", "dog", "fish"]
pets[1] = "hamster"
print(pets)  # ["cat", "hamster", "fish"]
```
